newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil traders hear scattered talk of U.S. sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil traders hear scattered talk of U.S. sales.

text.p: Rumors that Brazil was selling soybeans and soymeal to U.S. buyers were still alive but waned since Cargill Inc announced it would bring Brazilian beans to the U.S. for processing, traders here said.

"I haven't heard about any soymeal trades but I heard the U.S. bought soybeans, about four or five vessels," said a soymeal trader. This reportedly included two Cargill vessels destined for the U.S. and three for another large export firm, he added.
"They are said to be loading now, in June, at Paranagua," the trader said.
After the Cargill deal, there was talk of other vessels heading for the U.S., said a trader in key growing state of Rio Grande do Sul, but since then things had quietened down.
"The enthusiasm about the U.S. importing beans from Brazil has waned a little bit. Right at this moment, there's nothing new," he said.

Commenting on talk that California livestock producers were interested in South American soymeal, he said, "It seems kind of strange. I guess they could always take it to the Gulf and track it (ship it by rail)."
One broker reported talk that small U.S. crushers were importing a total of 50,000 tonnes soybeans from Brazil, but said he had no further information on the reported deals.
